--- title: Relational data and PostgreSQL — understand the model before connecting description: Evolve the in-memory task model, start an exclusively owned PostgreSQL cluster, distinguish processes, storage, databases and roles, and verify keys, constraints, NULL and recovery. --- import { getRelationalExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. A database is not an upgraded JSON file The H-series in-memory API can answer HTTP requests, but two requests can read the same old state and overwrite each other's changes. Process exit loses memory. Replacing memory with a JSON file changes the storage location, not the coordination problem: who manages simultaneous writers, recovers a partially completed write, or rejects invalid data written by a different script? Files work well for small tools with explicit single-writer ownership; increasing their size does not gradually turn them into collaborative storage. A relational database delegates these responsibilities to a separate server: typed records, relationships, constraints applied to every writer, concurrency coordination, and commit/recovery protocols. It is not a library for editing a JSON file directly, and it does not discover your business rules or permissions automatically. D01 establishes the model and server; D02 teaches queries; D03 groups changes into transactions. | Chapter contract | Verifiable scope | | --- | --- | | Prerequisites | L00–L14 and H01–H06; exceptions, modules, files, tests and the in-memory HTTP lab, but no assumed SQL or operations experience | | New capabilities | Draw relationships; explain tables, rows, keys, constraints and NULL; distinguish processes, directories, databases, roles and connections | | Independent acceptance | Create the model in an isolated cluster, predict who rejects invalid records, and design keys and relationships for a new entity | | Exclusions | Docker, ORM, migrations framework, authentication, pools and production deployment; successful installation is not modeling proficiency | Download the [complete D01 lab](/learning-assets/js2py/d01-relational-data.zip) and work inside the extracted `d01-relational-data` directory. All SQL, server and file operations run locally, not in browser Python. Displayed source and the download use the same lab files. ## 2. Make field evolution an explicit design decision The H model, `id/title/minutes/done/note`, describes single-user in-memory tasks. We now need to express who created a task in which project. The following changes are deliberate. **This creates a new practice database; it does not migrate existing H-series data.** | Previous field or new need | Relational choice | Reason and limit | | --- | --- | --- | | id | bigint identity primary key | Database allocation, not an array position; neither consecutive IDs nor preservation of memory IDs is promised | | title | At most 120 characters, non-NULL, not only ASCII spaces | Application validation remains useful; the database protects the minimum invariant | | minutes | Retained nonnegative estimate | Useful for aggregation and concurrency; a retained extension, not a mandatory capstone field | | done | status: todo / doing / done | false can map to todo and true to done; doing is new; do not maintain two conflicting truths | | note | Nullable description, at most 2000 characters | NULL means not supplied; empty text means supplied but empty | | Collaboration | users, projects, project_members | A user row is not authentication, and membership does not implement API authorization | | Ownership/time | project_id, created_by, due_at, created_at, updated_at | Explicit references; timestamptz for instants, UTC display in lab connections | `users.login` identifies fixture people; this is not a login system. Password hashes, tokens and authentication versions are absent. Add those through later migrations rather than inventing fake default passwords for an ORM example. Here `updated_at` has an insertion default only. Update code must maintain it; the column's name does not make it automatic. ## 3. One row represents a fact; keys express relationships A table specifies columns and types. A row is one record, without an inherent position in storage or query output. A primary key is unique and non-NULL and identifies the record across reorderings. Using a UI array index would identify a different item after sorting. Identity generates candidate numbers; PRIMARY KEY enforces uniqueness. ```text users (1) ----< projects.created_by users (1) ----< project_members >---- (1) projects users (1) ----< tasks.created_by projects (1) ----< tasks.project_id ``` The `<` side can contain many rows. A project has many tasks; each task belongs to one project. Users and projects form a many-to-many relationship, represented by two one-to-many relationships through `project_members`. Its composite primary key `(project_id, user_id)` allows a particular user to join a particular project once, while still joining other projects. `role` describes that membership, not the user's global identity. A foreign key stores the other record's ID instead of copying a user object into each task. Copies could disagree after a rename: an update anomaly. D02 will use JOIN to retrieve display names. A database need not store the exact shape of your presentation JSON. All references use `ON DELETE RESTRICT`: a project with tasks or memberships cannot be deleted silently along with its dependents. A complete deletion policy belongs in an explicit service operation. Equally important, a foreign key proves existence, not that the creator is a member or that the current HTTP caller has permission. Cross-table rules such as requiring an owner or making that owner the creator are not fully guaranteed by this DDL.
Explanation answer: why not store member_ids on projects or copy project_name into every task? An array makes both per-membership roles and unique project/user pairs harder to express through the constraints introduced here. Copying project names introduces update anomalies. A membership row represents one fact; its composite key and two foreign keys each enforce a separate rule. This is not a ban on arrays or JSON: independently constrained, queryable facts benefit from explicit relations in this model.
## 4. Understand DDL and constraints before memorizing insert order DDL is SQL that defines structure. `CREATE TABLE` creates a table; declarations describe permitted values; commas separate columns or table constraints, and a semicolon ends a statement. This complete schema is identical in all three labs. No ORM prerequisite is needed. {getRelationalExample('sql/schema.sql')} Read from parents outward: users, then projects referencing users, then memberships and tasks. Definition order does not nest tables; the referenced table must exist. `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` means ordinary inserts omit id. `DEFAULT` supplies an omitted column, not an explicitly supplied NULL. Omitting status produces todo; supplying NULL violates NOT NULL. | Rule | What it rejects | What it does not replace | | --- | --- | --- | | NOT NULL | Missing NULL values | Does not reject empty text | | CHECK | A false row expression, such as negative minutes | Alone it does not reject an unknown result caused by NULL | | UNIQUE | Duplicate login identifiers | This schema is case-sensitive; alice and Alice differ | | PRIMARY KEY | Duplicate or NULL identity, possibly across columns | Does not mean the entire business record is complete | | FOREIGN KEY | A reference to a missing parent | Neither creates the parent nor proves authorization | | varchar(n) | An ordinary write exceeding the length | Not every application normalization rule | `btrim` removes ordinary spaces by default, not Python `strip()`'s entire Unicode whitespace set. The application may be stricter; do not claim identical validation. `timestamptz` represents an instant; display depends on the connection timezone and does not preserve the originally entered timezone name. The lab uses UTC and does not resolve product calendar or daylight-saving requirements. ## 5. NULL is neither empty text nor JavaScript undefined SQL NULL means missing or unknown. A Python driver usually reads it as `None`, but SQL comparison does not work like Python comparison: `NULL = NULL` is unknown, not true. WHERE retains only true conditions. Test missingness with `IS NULL`. Replacing every missing value with empty text destroys information. Observe that tasks 1 and 4 have NULL descriptions while task 2 has empty text. A `CHECK (minutes >= 0)` does not become false for NULL, so tasks also needs NOT NULL. The tests create a temporary CHECK-only table, actually insert NULL, and compare that success with the tasks rejection. Constraint names alone are not the lesson. ## 6. Six objects between installed software and a running database | Object | Responsibility | Common misconception | | --- | --- | --- | | Tool binaries | postgres is the server executable; psql is a command-line client | Running psql does not prove a server is running | | Server process | Accept connections, execute queries, coordinate concurrency and persistence | Python exiting does not stop the server | | Data directory / cluster | initdb creates catalogs and database storage; cluster here does not mean multiple machines | Never edit its binary files or initialize over an existing directory | | Database | A logical database within the cluster, named langshift_lab here | Not a separate OS process | | Role | PostgreSQL's permission identity; lab_student is an ordinary role | Not the OS username or a row of the users table | | Connection | Stateful client/server communication establishing a database session | A connection string is an address/options description, not a live connection or transaction | Data flows from terminal/driver through a socket to the server session, constraints and storage, then back as results or errors. A Unix socket is a local communication endpoint, not the database file. The port number also identifies the socket filename here, although TCP is disabled. A random administrator role bootstraps the cluster; ordinary SQL runs as non-superuser `lab_student`. Owning this practice database is not a production privilege design. ## 7. Prepare step by step without touching existing databases Verified **2026-09-28**. Fixed baseline: PostgreSQL **18.6** (official release date 2026-08-13), CPython **3.13.15**, uv **0.12.13**, pytest **8.4.2**, psycopg **3.3.6**. The macOS Homebrew tools already exist on this machine; no system installation is needed. Elsewhere, obtain matching binaries through the official PostgreSQL download entry and verify their paths. Installation on other operating systems was not tested; do not blindly reuse the Homebrew path. **Step one: inspect binaries, not default services.** `PG_BIN` is a directory, not a DSN. Do not use `brew services`, unqualified management commands without `-D`, or assumptions about who owns a service on port 5432. **Connection-environment checkpoint.** libpq can read defaults beyond the socket in a DSN: for example `PGHOSTADDR` selects a network address and `PGSERVICE` loads a saved connection profile. Therefore the controller refuses every inherited `PG*` name except `PG_BIN` (the tool directory) and `PGHOST` (overridden by the explicit private socket), before startup or SQL. It reports variable names, never their values. If refused, inspect and remove only those settings in this lab shell, then retry; do not substitute a production DSN or blindly reset an existing database. `DATABASE_URL` remains ignored. The controller supplies its own empty mode-0600 password file instead of reading a user credential file, and strips database defaults from child processes. Even a polluted shell can run `status`/`stop` to clean up this owned cluster; stop still verifies the saved server identity. The translated README explains the same policy. **Test counts.** This lab has 14 business/SQL cases plus 50 environment-boundary cases (64 total). The latter include parametrized rejected settings, private-passfile validation and owned-loopback probes. They protect the experiment; they are not 50 new SQL topics or proof of production security. ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928 export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928 export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin "$PG_BIN/postgres" --version "$PG_BIN/psql" --version "$PG_BIN/initdb" --version "$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version uv --version uv sync --locked uv run --locked python --version ``` All four PostgreSQL commands should contain `18.6 (Homebrew)`; uv should report 0.12.13 and Python 3.13.15. `uv sync --locked` creates this lab's `.venv` from a public-PyPI lockfile, without updating it or installing frontend dependencies. Stop on a version mismatch rather than mixing baselines. **Step two: allocate exclusive storage and start an exclusive process.** The controller automates explicit steps rather than replacing them with magic: allocate `/tmp/lsdb-*` with mkdtemp; set root and socket directories to 0700; write an ownership marker; initialize the new directory with `initdb -D`; set `listen_addresses = ''`; start with `pg_ctl` using an explicit data directory and log; create the role and database only through this socket. The random port and unique directory never reuse an existing service. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py start uv run --locked python labctl.py status uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql ``` The first start prints a random root, and status should show running as true. Reset prints the following fixed output. It deletes and recreates **this lab's four tables**; it is not read-only. Save your own SQL files before resetting an exercise. ```text schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5 ``` **Step three: understand the address before opening a connection.** The DSN contains `host=/private/tmp/lsdb-.../socket`, a random port, `dbname=langshift_lab`, `user=lab_student`, UTC and timeout options. macOS may resolve /tmp to /private/tmp; the abbreviated address in this paragraph is not copyable configuration. There is no password because local trust is bounded by private directory permissions and disabled TCP. Processes under the same OS account, and root, are not isolated from it. This is emphatically not production trust guidance. Before connecting or resetting, the controller checks the marker, directory ownership, server data directory, system identifier and `server_version_num=180006`. It deliberately ignores DATABASE_URL. Do not redirect it to your own database. psql backslash commands are interpreted by the client, not by the SQL server. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py psql ``` ```sql \conninfo SELECT current_database(), current_user; \dt \d tasks SELECT id, title, status, minutes FROM tasks ORDER BY id; \q ``` `\conninfo` shows the connection, `\dt` lists tables, `\d tasks` inspects constraints, and `\q` exits the client without stopping the server. A continuation prompt such as `langshift_lab-#` often means you have not terminated the statement with a semicolon. Ctrl+C abandons that input; rebuilding the cluster is not the remedy. ## 8. Populate the structure with observable facts {getRelationalExample('sql/seed.sql')} The seed relies on empty-table identities starting at 1, so use reset rather than pasting it repeatedly into an arbitrary database. Expect Alice and Bob, Launch/Docs/Empty, four memberships and five tasks. Empty has no tasks but does have an owner. A foreign-key integer makes the server verify a parent record; the number itself carries no inferred business meaning. {getRelationalExample('sql/inspect.sql')} Inspection renders NULL as `(null)` to distinguish empty text. Tasks appear as `Design API / Add tests / Ship demo / Read SQL / Write guide`, with minutes `30 / 45 / 15 / 20 / 40`. This is the current ordered seed, not a promise about queries without ORDER BY. ## 9. Deliberate failures: who rejects what, and what remains? Reset first, then execute the explicitly failing experiment. {getRelationalExample('sql/expected_failures.sql')} ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql uv run --locked pytest -q ``` The four INSERT statements fail at server execution: duplicate login gives `23505`, nonexistent user_id `23503`, negative minutes `23514`, NULL title `23502`. ERROR output is expected, not evidence that nothing ran. This file temporarily disables psql's stop-on-error behavior and proceeds statement by statement; the final task count remains 5. In psql's default autocommit mode each statement finishes independently, so a failed statement cannot undo an earlier independently committed statement. D03 tests grouping them into one rollback unit. Tests also cover overlong titles (`22001`) and deletion of a referenced project. In the **actual 18.6 run**, `ON DELETE RESTRICT` returns `RestrictViolation / 23001`; do not assume every referential error is `23503`. Inserting a nonexistent foreign key still yields `23503`. SQLSTATE is more suitable for precise assertions than localized message text.
Guided modification answer: to allow unknown estimates, should you only remove CHECK? No. NOT NULL prohibits NULL; CHECK prohibits negative values. Allowing unknown estimates requires removing NOT NULL while retaining the nonnegative CHECK, and reconsidering whether default 0 remains appropriate. Compare NULL, 0 and -1 in a separate practice table rather than silently changing the three-lab contract. Later aggregation must distinguish zero from unknown; coalescing both to zero requires an explicit business choice.
## 10. Independent variation: multiple comments on a task Design `task_comments` independently: each comment belongs to an existing task and is written by an existing user; body is nonblank and at most 500 characters; a user may comment on the same task multiple times; deleting a referenced task is initially restricted. # d01-relational-data — Relational models, database objects and constraints

Verified 2026-09-28. A standalone lab using real PostgreSQL, not SQLite or browser Python. The full three-language lesson is `module-21-relational-data`.

## Outcome and prerequisites

Prerequisites: L00–L14 and H01–H06; D02 additionally requires D01, D03 requires D02. D01 does not assume SQL or operations knowledge. Read the lesson's mechanisms before following this reproducibility guide; installation alone is not mastery.

This lab verifies relational models, database objects and constraints. `model-contract.json` records `d01-d03-v1`, and `sql/schema.sql` is the executable DDL. User fixtures are not login accounts. H's done explicitly becomes status (todo/doing/done), note becomes nullable description, and nonnegative estimate minutes is retained. Users, projects, memberships and time fields are new. No existing in-memory data is automatically migrated.

## Fixed environment, no system service installation

- PostgreSQL 18.6 (Homebrew here; actual server_version_num=180006), officially released 2026-08-13.
- CPython 3.13.15, uv 0.12.13, pytest 8.4.2, psycopg[binary] 3.3.6.
- requires-python >=3.13,<3.14; uv package=false; a real public-PyPI uv.lock.
- Only macOS/Homebrew execution was tested. Other OS installation, TCP/TLS and production configuration were not. No Docker, ORM, authentication or frontend dependencies.

Work inside extracted `d01-relational-data`, not its parent. Tools already exist on this machine. **Do not run brew services, connect to default port 5432, or initialize existing storage.**

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928
export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin
"$PG_BIN/postgres" --version
"$PG_BIN/initdb" --version
"$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version
"$PG_BIN/psql" --version
uv --version
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked python --version
```

Stop on a version mismatch. PG_BIN is a binary directory. psql is the client, postgres the server, initdb creates new storage, and pg_ctl manages the explicitly selected data directory's process. Installed binaries, running processes and data directories are different objects.

## Own an isolated cluster and database

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn
uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset
```

Start allocates a short `/tmp/lsdb-*` path (possibly displayed as /private/tmp on macOS), sets root/socket permissions to 0700, saves matching state and marker files, initializes new storage, disables TCP, chooses a private-socket port, and starts pg_ctl with explicit -D and server.log. A random administrator creates database langshift_lab and ordinary role lab_student. A database is a logical namespace inside the cluster; a role is a database identity, not a users-table record. The socket is an endpoint, a DSN describes the address/options, and a connection is an active session.

Passwordless local trust is for the private directory with TCP disabled only. Processes under the same OS account and root are not isolated. Never copy this policy into an exposed or production server. Ownership is checked before connection/reset/stop; SQL connections additionally verify server data directory, system identifier and version. DATABASE_URL is ignored and arbitrary remote DSNs are not accepted. Do not remove those protections.

Reset **destructively recreates the four owned lab tables**, printing `schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5`. Every business pytest case and D03 demo scenario also resets. Do not run competing runners or keep business data here. Stop/start retains committed data; OS cleanup of /tmp means this is still neither permanent storage nor backup.

## PostgreSQL environment boundary

`labctl.py` itself checks the environment before startup or any SQL connection, including direct Python imports: **all `PG*` variables except `PG_BIN` and `PGHOST` are rejected**, even empty or unknown names. This deliberately also rejects explicitly overridden variables such as `PGPORT`, `PGUSER` and `PGDATABASE`, not just `PGHOSTADDR`, `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, `PGPASSFILE`, `PGPASSWORD` or `PGOPTIONS`. Errors list variable **names only**, never their values. Unset the reported variables in your lab shell before starting or running SQL; do not copy service settings or credentials into this lab.

`PG_BIN` still selects the tool directory. `PGHOST` remains accepted but ignored because every DSN explicitly selects the owned private socket; the maintenance runner's `PGHOST=/nonexistent/...` check remains valid. `DATABASE_URL` is still ignored. All child processes (including initdb, pg_ctl and psql) receive an environment without any `PG*` variables or `DATABASE_URL`; tool paths and data paths are explicit. Python connections do not temporarily mutate the process environment, so D03's concurrent connections do not race over environment restoration.

Every administrator/student DSN explicitly selects the owned root's **empty, mode-0600 `empty.pgpass`**, not the user's default `~/.pgpass`. It is created for new or previously owned clusters; symlink, nonempty, wrong-owner, nonregular or wrong-mode files are refused. psql also uses `-X -w` (no startup file or password prompt). The random administrator and server data-directory/system-identifier/version checks are retained; no business SQL is changed.

**Bad connection environment does not block cleanup:** `status` uses clean pg_ctl calls, and `stop` performs the same server identity check in a clean Python child before stopping the explicitly owned data directory. It does not bypass marker/PID/identity failures. After stopping, remove the reported variables before restarting. An exported `dsn` is descriptive, not a sandbox: do not pass it to an arbitrary client with inherited connection defaults; use `labctl.py psql` instead.

`tests/test_environment.py` adds 50 cases: pre-connection/pre-start mock refusals, subprocess environment checks, passfile checks, standalone CLI refusals against our own loopback listener, private-socket PGHOST/DATABASE_URL compatibility, and poisoned-environment stop/status/restart recovery. These cases override the business tests' automatic SQL reset so negative tests do not open a connection first. They exercise selected failure paths, not every possible attack; same-OS-user/root process or file tampering is outside this lab's isolation boundary.

## Execute, interpret and verify

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql
uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql
uv run --locked pytest -q
```

Expect **64 passed** (14 existing business cases + 50 environment cases), with variable duration. ERROR output in intentionally failing SQL is expected; unexpected command failure must not be ignored. D01 checks duplicate 23505, bad foreign key 23503, CHECK 23514, NULL 23502, length 22001 and this version's delete RESTRICT 23001. D02 stores attack payloads literally without dropping tasks, and rejects invalid sorting/pagination in Python. D03 checks second-step 23503, subsequent-query 25P02, zero residue after rollback, real read-committed [30,40], repeatable-read [30,30], lost update 37, atomic increments 42, a one-row uniqueness race, lock timeout 55P03, and old-snapshot update 40001 followed by a whole-unit retry to 42.

The lesson contains exact demo output. D02's fixed ID requires reset first; D03 resets each scenario itself. These tests are execution, not compilation: an actual server applies constraints, parameters, transactions and locks. Independent exercise references are in answers; attempt them before looking. They are not extra baseline schema or HTTP integration.

## File responsibilities

- labctl.py: exclusive startup, address/identity checks, reset, psql and stop; no global service management.
- sql/schema.sql and sql/seed.sql: identical three-lab schema and deterministic fixture; model-contract records the DDL hash.
- sql/*.sql: queries or explicitly labeled failure experiments.
- tests/ and conftest.py: reset only the owned database per business case, including reference-variation execution.
- answers/: references for independent work, not the starting point.
- pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version, .env.example: dependencies/configuration; env.example is documentation, not automatically loaded.
- Three READMEs, sources.json and model-contract.json: reproducibility, provenance and ORM handoff.
- FILES.json: packaged file allowlist; the repository's sibling ../d01-relational-data-files.json drives integration packaging. No data directories, .lab-state.json, .venv, caches or credentials belong in the archive.

## Safe shutdown and recovery

```bash
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
uv run --locked python labctl.py status
uv run --locked python labctl.py start
uv run --locked python labctl.py stop
```

Stop checks the marker, PID-directory relationship and healthy server identity before fast shutdown of its explicit -D, then waits. Status reports running=false and pg_ctl_status=3. Fast shutdown disconnects this cluster's clients, rolls back uncommitted work and retains committed data/logs. It never signals unrelated postgres processes, invokes brew services or deletes directories. Start after stop resumes storage, not initdb.

For connection failure inspect status and the printed root's server.log; for version mismatch inspect PG_BIN; for missing tables check preparation. Ownership/identity mismatch refuses reset and stop: investigate rather than deleting markers or substituting a user database. Partial first startup attempts to stop only its newly allocated directory and preserves the error. Inspect status/logs before proceeding; never reinitialize old storage. When a health/identity check itself is impossible, the controller refuses rather than guessing. Never use killall as a fallback.

At a break, record lab path, root, last command, tests, SQLSTATE and next action. After OS cleanup of /tmp, begin with a fresh extraction rather than treating unmarked old data as a new cluster.

## Limits and official sources

Normal stop/start is not disaster recovery. No production backup restore, power loss, ambiguous network commit, full Serializable matrix, real deadlock, authentication, authorization, pooling or load test is claimed. Later ORM work must preserve constraint names/types and failure tests. updated_at is not automatic. Owner existence and creator authorization are not fully enforced by foreign keys.

Official sources checked 2026-09-28. psycopg's docs site returned 403, so the official repository's fixed 3.3.6 documentation sources were read. PostgreSQL 18 docs and the 18.6 release page were accessible.


本地 trust 僅因目錄私有且 TCP 禁止才用於無密碼練習；同一 OS 用戶下的進程和 root 不在隔離範圍內，不能複製到公網或生產。連接、reset、stop 都驗證所有權；SQL 連接還驗證服務端數據目錄、系統標識和版本。腳本忽略 DATABASE_URL，不接受任意遠端 DSN；不要修改這些防護。

## PostgreSQL 環境邊界

`labctl.py` 自身在啟動或任何 SQL 連接前檢查環境，直接透過 Python 匯入呼叫也一樣：**拒絕除 `PG_BIN`、`PGHOST` 外的全部 `PG*` 變數**，包括空值和未知名稱。這也會保守拒絕雖已被顯式覆蓋的 `PGPORT`、`PGUSER`、`PGDATABASE`，不只 `PGHOSTADDR`、`PGSERVICE`、`PGSERVICEFILE`、`PGPASSFILE`、`PGPASSWORD`、`PGOPTIONS`。錯誤只列變數**名**，不列印值。啟動或執行 SQL 前，在實驗 shell 中 unset 報出的變數；不要把其他服務設定或憑證複製進實驗。

`PG_BIN` 仍用於選擇工具目錄。`PGHOST` 仍被接受但忽略，因為每條 DSN 都顯式指定自有私有 socket；維護 runner 的 `PGHOST=/nonexistent/...` 驗證仍成立。`DATABASE_URL` 仍忽略。所有子行程（包括 initdb、pg_ctl、psql）都使用清除全部 `PG*` 和 `DATABASE_URL` 的環境，工具和資料路徑顯式指定。Python 連接不暫時修改行程環境，因此 D03 並行連接不存在環境還原競態。

管理員和學生的每條 DSN 均顯式指定自有 root 下**內容為空、權限 0600 的 `empty.pgpass`**，不使用預設 `~/.pgpass`。新集群和已有自有集群均可建立該檔案；符號連結、非空、擁有者錯誤、非一般檔案或權限錯誤均拒絕。psql 同時使用 `-X -w`（不讀啟動檔案、不提示輸入密碼）。隨機管理員及伺服器資料目錄／系統識別碼／版本核驗保留，不改業務 SQL。

**錯誤的連接環境不阻止清理：** `status` 使用乾淨環境呼叫 pg_ctl；`stop` 在乾淨 Python 子行程中完成相同的伺服器身分核驗，再停止顯式指定的自有資料目錄。不會繞過 marker／PID／身分檢查失敗。停止後須清除報出的變數才能重新 start。匯出的 `dsn` 只是連接描述，不是沙箱：不要交給繼承其他連接預設值的任意客戶端；請使用 `labctl.py psql`。

--- title: Relational data and PostgreSQL — understand the model before connecting description: Evolve the in-memory task model, start an exclusively owned PostgreSQL cluster, distinguish processes, storage, databases and roles, and verify keys, constraints, NULL and recovery. --- import { getRelationalExample } from '@/lib/js2py-examples' ## 1. A database is not an upgraded JSON file The H-series in-memory API can answer HTTP requests, but two requests can read the same old state and overwrite each other's changes. Process exit loses memory. Replacing memory with a JSON file changes the storage location, not the coordination problem: who manages simultaneous writers, recovers a partially completed write, or rejects invalid data written by a different script? Files work well for small tools with explicit single-writer ownership; increasing their size does not gradually turn them into collaborative storage. A relational database delegates these responsibilities to a separate server: typed records, relationships, constraints applied to every writer, concurrency coordination, and commit/recovery protocols. It is not a library for editing a JSON file directly, and it does not discover your business rules or permissions automatically. D01 establishes the model and server; D02 teaches queries; D03 groups changes into transactions. | Chapter contract | Verifiable scope | | --- | --- | | Prerequisites | L00–L14 and H01–H06; exceptions, modules, files, tests and the in-memory HTTP lab, but no assumed SQL or operations experience | | New capabilities | Draw relationships; explain tables, rows, keys, constraints and NULL; distinguish processes, directories, databases, roles and connections | | Independent acceptance | Create the model in an isolated cluster, predict who rejects invalid records, and design keys and relationships for a new entity | | Exclusions | Docker, ORM, migrations framework, authentication, pools and production deployment; successful installation is not modeling proficiency | Download the [complete D01 lab](/learning-assets/js2py/d01-relational-data.zip) and work inside the extracted `d01-relational-data` directory. All SQL, server and file operations run locally, not in browser Python. Displayed source and the download use the same lab files. ## 2. Make field evolution an explicit design decision The H model, `id/title/minutes/done/note`, describes single-user in-memory tasks. We now need to express who created a task in which project. The following changes are deliberate. **This creates a new practice database; it does not migrate existing H-series data.** | Previous field or new need | Relational choice | Reason and limit | | --- | --- | --- | | id | bigint identity primary key | Database allocation, not an array position; neither consecutive IDs nor preservation of memory IDs is promised | | title | At most 120 characters, non-NULL, not only ASCII spaces | Application validation remains useful; the database protects the minimum invariant | | minutes | Retained nonnegative estimate | Useful for aggregation and concurrency; a retained extension, not a mandatory capstone field | | done | status: todo / doing / done | false can map to todo and true to done; doing is new; do not maintain two conflicting truths | | note | Nullable description, at most 2000 characters | NULL means not supplied; empty text means supplied but empty | | Collaboration | users, projects, project_members | A user row is not authentication, and membership does not implement API authorization | | Ownership/time | project_id, created_by, due_at, created_at, updated_at | Explicit references; timestamptz for instants, UTC display in lab connections | `users.login` identifies fixture people; this is not a login system. Password hashes, tokens and authentication versions are absent. Add those through later migrations rather than inventing fake default passwords for an ORM example. Here `updated_at` has an insertion default only. Update code must maintain it; the column's name does not make it automatic. ## 3. One row represents a fact; keys express relationships A table specifies columns and types. A row is one record, without an inherent position in storage or query output. A primary key is unique and non-NULL and identifies the record across reorderings. Using a UI array index would identify a different item after sorting. Identity generates candidate numbers; PRIMARY KEY enforces uniqueness. ```text users (1) ----< projects.created_by users (1) ----< project_members >---- (1) projects users (1) ----< tasks.created_by projects (1) ----< tasks.project_id ``` The `<` side can contain many rows. A project has many tasks; each task belongs to one project. Users and projects form a many-to-many relationship, represented by two one-to-many relationships through `project_members`. Its composite primary key `(project_id, user_id)` allows a particular user to join a particular project once, while still joining other projects. `role` describes that membership, not the user's global identity. A foreign key stores the other record's ID instead of copying a user object into each task. Copies could disagree after a rename: an update anomaly. D02 will use JOIN to retrieve display names. A database need not store the exact shape of your presentation JSON. All references use `ON DELETE RESTRICT`: a project with tasks or memberships cannot be deleted silently along with its dependents. A complete deletion policy belongs in an explicit service operation. Equally important, a foreign key proves existence, not that the creator is a member or that the current HTTP caller has permission. Cross-table rules such as requiring an owner or making that owner the creator are not fully guaranteed by this DDL.
Explanation answer: why not store member_ids on projects or copy project_name into every task? An array makes both per-membership roles and unique project/user pairs harder to express through the constraints introduced here. Copying project names introduces update anomalies. A membership row represents one fact; its composite key and two foreign keys each enforce a separate rule. This is not a ban on arrays or JSON: independently constrained, queryable facts benefit from explicit relations in this model.
## 4. Understand DDL and constraints before memorizing insert order DDL is SQL that defines structure. `CREATE TABLE` creates a table; declarations describe permitted values; commas separate columns or table constraints, and a semicolon ends a statement. This complete schema is identical in all three labs. No ORM prerequisite is needed. {getRelationalExample('sql/schema.sql')} Read from parents outward: users, then projects referencing users, then memberships and tasks. Definition order does not nest tables; the referenced table must exist. `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` means ordinary inserts omit id. `DEFAULT` supplies an omitted column, not an explicitly supplied NULL. Omitting status produces todo; supplying NULL violates NOT NULL. | Rule | What it rejects | What it does not replace | | --- | --- | --- | | NOT NULL | Missing NULL values | Does not reject empty text | | CHECK | A false row expression, such as negative minutes | Alone it does not reject an unknown result caused by NULL | | UNIQUE | Duplicate login identifiers | This schema is case-sensitive; alice and Alice differ | | PRIMARY KEY | Duplicate or NULL identity, possibly across columns | Does not mean the entire business record is complete | | FOREIGN KEY | A reference to a missing parent | Neither creates the parent nor proves authorization | | varchar(n) | An ordinary write exceeding the length | Not every application normalization rule | `btrim` removes ordinary spaces by default, not Python `strip()`'s entire Unicode whitespace set. The application may be stricter; do not claim identical validation. `timestamptz` represents an instant; display depends on the connection timezone and does not preserve the originally entered timezone name. The lab uses UTC and does not resolve product calendar or daylight-saving requirements. ## 5. NULL is neither empty text nor JavaScript undefined SQL NULL means missing or unknown. A Python driver usually reads it as `None`, but SQL comparison does not work like Python comparison: `NULL = NULL` is unknown, not true. WHERE retains only true conditions. Test missingness with `IS NULL`. Replacing every missing value with empty text destroys information. Observe that tasks 1 and 4 have NULL descriptions while task 2 has empty text. A `CHECK (minutes >= 0)` does not become false for NULL, so tasks also needs NOT NULL. The tests create a temporary CHECK-only table, actually insert NULL, and compare that success with the tasks rejection. Constraint names alone are not the lesson. ## 6. Six objects between installed software and a running database | Object | Responsibility | Common misconception | | --- | --- | --- | | Tool binaries | postgres is the server executable; psql is a command-line client | Running psql does not prove a server is running | | Server process | Accept connections, execute queries, coordinate concurrency and persistence | Python exiting does not stop the server | | Data directory / cluster | initdb creates catalogs and database storage; cluster here does not mean multiple machines | Never edit its binary files or initialize over an existing directory | | Database | A logical database within the cluster, named langshift_lab here | Not a separate OS process | | Role | PostgreSQL's permission identity; lab_student is an ordinary role | Not the OS username or a row of the users table | | Connection | Stateful client/server communication establishing a database session | A connection string is an address/options description, not a live connection or transaction | Data flows from terminal/driver through a socket to the server session, constraints and storage, then back as results or errors. A Unix socket is a local communication endpoint, not the database file. The port number also identifies the socket filename here, although TCP is disabled. A random administrator role bootstraps the cluster; ordinary SQL runs as non-superuser `lab_student`. Owning this practice database is not a production privilege design. ## 7. Prepare step by step without touching existing databases Verified **2026-09-28**. Fixed baseline: PostgreSQL **18.6** (official release date 2026-08-13), CPython **3.13.15**, uv **0.12.13**, pytest **8.4.2**, psycopg **3.3.6**. The macOS Homebrew tools already exist on this machine; no system installation is needed. Elsewhere, obtain matching binaries through the official PostgreSQL download entry and verify their paths. Installation on other operating systems was not tested; do not blindly reuse the Homebrew path. **Step one: inspect binaries, not default services.** `PG_BIN` is a directory, not a DSN. Do not use `brew services`, unqualified management commands without `-D`, or assumptions about who owns a service on port 5432. **Connection-environment checkpoint.** libpq can read defaults beyond the socket in a DSN: for example `PGHOSTADDR` selects a network address and `PGSERVICE` loads a saved connection profile. Therefore the controller refuses every inherited `PG*` name except `PG_BIN` (the tool directory) and `PGHOST` (overridden by the explicit private socket), before startup or SQL. It reports variable names, never their values. If refused, inspect and remove only those settings in this lab shell, then retry; do not substitute a production DSN or blindly reset an existing database. `DATABASE_URL` remains ignored. The controller supplies its own empty mode-0600 password file instead of reading a user credential file, and strips database defaults from child processes. Even a polluted shell can run `status`/`stop` to clean up this owned cluster; stop still verifies the saved server identity. The translated README explains the same policy. **Test counts.** This lab has 14 business/SQL cases plus 50 environment-boundary cases (64 total). The latter include parametrized rejected settings, private-passfile validation and owned-loopback probes. They protect the experiment; they are not 50 new SQL topics or proof of production security. ```bash export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" export UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-python-20260928 export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/langshift-js2py-uv-cache-20260928 export PG_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin "$PG_BIN/postgres" --version "$PG_BIN/psql" --version "$PG_BIN/initdb" --version "$PG_BIN/pg_ctl" --version uv --version uv sync --locked uv run --locked python --version ``` All four PostgreSQL commands should contain `18.6 (Homebrew)`; uv should report 0.12.13 and Python 3.13.15. `uv sync --locked` creates this lab's `.venv` from a public-PyPI lockfile, without updating it or installing frontend dependencies. Stop on a version mismatch rather than mixing baselines. **Step two: allocate exclusive storage and start an exclusive process.** The controller automates explicit steps rather than replacing them with magic: allocate `/tmp/lsdb-*` with mkdtemp; set root and socket directories to 0700; write an ownership marker; initialize the new directory with `initdb -D`; set `listen_addresses = ''`; start with `pg_ctl` using an explicit data directory and log; create the role and database only through this socket. The random port and unique directory never reuse an existing service. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py start uv run --locked python labctl.py status uv run --locked python labctl.py dsn uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql ``` The first start prints a random root, and status should show running as true. Reset prints the following fixed output. It deletes and recreates **this lab's four tables**; it is not read-only. Save your own SQL files before resetting an exercise. ```text schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5 ``` **Step three: understand the address before opening a connection.** The DSN contains `host=/private/tmp/lsdb-.../socket`, a random port, `dbname=langshift_lab`, `user=lab_student`, UTC and timeout options. macOS may resolve /tmp to /private/tmp; the abbreviated address in this paragraph is not copyable configuration. There is no password because local trust is bounded by private directory permissions and disabled TCP. Processes under the same OS account, and root, are not isolated from it. This is emphatically not production trust guidance. Before connecting or resetting, the controller checks the marker, directory ownership, server data directory, system identifier and `server_version_num=180006`. It deliberately ignores DATABASE_URL. Do not redirect it to your own database. psql backslash commands are interpreted by the client, not by the SQL server. ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py psql ``` ```sql \conninfo SELECT current_database(), current_user; \dt \d tasks SELECT id, title, status, minutes FROM tasks ORDER BY id; \q ``` `\conninfo` shows the connection, `\dt` lists tables, `\d tasks` inspects constraints, and `\q` exits the client without stopping the server. A continuation prompt such as `langshift_lab-#` often means you have not terminated the statement with a semicolon. Ctrl+C abandons that input; rebuilding the cluster is not the remedy. ## 8. Populate the structure with observable facts {getRelationalExample('sql/seed.sql')} The seed relies on empty-table identities starting at 1, so use reset rather than pasting it repeatedly into an arbitrary database. Expect Alice and Bob, Launch/Docs/Empty, four memberships and five tasks. Empty has no tasks but does have an owner. A foreign-key integer makes the server verify a parent record; the number itself carries no inferred business meaning. {getRelationalExample('sql/inspect.sql')} Inspection renders NULL as `(null)` to distinguish empty text. Tasks appear as `Design API / Add tests / Ship demo / Read SQL / Write guide`, with minutes `30 / 45 / 15 / 20 / 40`. This is the current ordered seed, not a promise about queries without ORDER BY. ## 9. Deliberate failures: who rejects what, and what remains? Reset first, then execute the explicitly failing experiment. {getRelationalExample('sql/expected_failures.sql')} ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py reset --yes-reset uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/expected_failures.sql uv run --locked pytest -q ``` The four INSERT statements fail at server execution: duplicate login gives `23505`, nonexistent user_id `23503`, negative minutes `23514`, NULL title `23502`. ERROR output is expected, not evidence that nothing ran. This file temporarily disables psql's stop-on-error behavior and proceeds statement by statement; the final task count remains 5. In psql's default autocommit mode each statement finishes independently, so a failed statement cannot undo an earlier independently committed statement. D03 tests grouping them into one rollback unit. Tests also cover overlong titles (`22001`) and deletion of a referenced project. In the **actual 18.6 run**, `ON DELETE RESTRICT` returns `RestrictViolation / 23001`; do not assume every referential error is `23503`. Inserting a nonexistent foreign key still yields `23503`. SQLSTATE is more suitable for precise assertions than localized message text.
Guided modification answer: to allow unknown estimates, should you only remove CHECK? No. NOT NULL prohibits NULL; CHECK prohibits negative values. Allowing unknown estimates requires removing NOT NULL while retaining the nonnegative CHECK, and reconsidering whether default 0 remains appropriate. Compare NULL, 0 and -1 in a separate practice table rather than silently changing the three-lab contract. Later aggregation must distinguish zero from unknown; coalescing both to zero requires an explicit business choice.
## 10. Independent variation: multiple comments on a task Design `task_comments` independently: each comment belongs to an existing task and is written by an existing user; body is nonblank and at most 500 characters; a user may comment on the same task multiple times; deleting a referenced task is initially restricted. Draw cardinalities, choose the key, write DDL and a successful INSERT, then produce missing-task and blank-body failures. Why is `(task_id, author_id)` not a suitable primary key? Open the answer only after attempting it. Explain each constraint; passing tests alone does not demonstrate understanding.
Independent variation reference and acceptance {getRelationalExample('answers/variant.sql')} Comments have their own identity and repeat authors are allowed, so use an independent identity primary key. The foreign keys protect task and author existence, not project permissions. `tests/test_variant.py` executes the reference DDL and checks both failures, then drops the exercise table so it does not interfere with model reset. This table is not part of the ORM baseline.
## 11. Shutdown, recovery and a resumable checkpoint ```bash uv run --locked python labctl.py stop uv run --locked python labctl.py status uv run --locked python labctl.py start uv run --locked python labctl.py psql --file sql/inspect.sql uv run --locked python labctl.py stop ``` After checking markers and server identity, stop invokes `pg_ctl -m fast -w stop` against only its own `-D`: disconnect this cluster's clients, roll back uncommitted transactions, and shut down. Other clusters are untouched. Status should show `running: false` and `pg_ctl_status: 3`. Start reuses the data directory without reinitializing it. Without reset, committed records should remain. This is a normal stop/start persistence check, not a backup or disaster-recovery drill. Data and logs are retained for diagnosis. The OS may clean /tmp, so it is not durable long-term storage. Do not copy a live data directory as a backup, delete ownership markers to bypass protection, or kill every postgres process. | Symptom | First inspection | Recovery boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Missing/wrong binaries | PG_BIN and all four version commands | No automatic system installation or service upgrade | | Connection refused/missing socket | This lab's status and root/server.log | Start only the owned cluster | | Marker/identity mismatch | .lab-state.json and the private marker | Reset and shutdown refuse; investigate instead of disabling checks | | Partial initialization | Start exception, private logs and status | Script attempts to stop only the directory just allocated; preserve evidence and do not reinitialize old storage | | Missing tables | Whether reset ran and which database is selected | Confirm the target before choosing a destructive reset | When pausing, record the lab directory, random root, last successful command, passed tests, outstanding SQLSTATE and next action. A useful checkpoint is schema/seed verified, 64 tests passing (14 business + 50 environment), cluster stopped. Resume with status/start rather than an automatic reset. ## 12. Acceptance and official references Without the answer, draw the four-table model, distinguish a database role from a business user, connect to your own database, predict at least three constraint failures, distinguish NULL from empty text, and prove committed data outlives Python memory through stop/start. The acceptance runner also rebuilds downloads from allowlists and executes against an exclusive cluster. MDX compilation does not prove these behaviors. Official references checked **2026-09-28**, using PostgreSQL 18 documentation and runtime 18.6: - [PostgreSQL 18.6 release notes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.6/): patch version and release date. - [Client/server architecture](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/tutorial-arch.html), [initdb](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/app-initdb.html), [pg_ctl](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/app-pg-ctl.html): objects and lifecycle. - [Constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-constraints.html), [error codes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/errcodes-appendix.html): relational rules and CHECK's NULL behavior. - [libpq connection parameters](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-connect.html), [official downloads](https://www.postgresql.org/download/): connection targets and tool distribution. Not validated: other OS installation, TCP/TLS or production roles, backup recovery, authentication/authorization and production capacity. None is an implicit promise of this lab.

"""Own one disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 cluster; never use DATABASE_URL.

All destructive operations are restricted to our marker-checked /tmp directory.
Stop retains files for recovery. Nothing invokes brew services, kill or rm -rf.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

import psycopg
from psycopg.conninfo import make_conninfo

LAB = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
STATE = LAB / ".lab-state.json"
MARKER = "langshift-owned-cluster.json"
VERSION_NUM = 180006


# PGHOST is safe only because every SQL DSN supplies an explicit private socket.
# PG_BIN selects executables, not a libpq connection parameter. Fail closed for
# all other PG* names (even empty/unknown ones), including future libpq defaults.
ALLOWED_PG_ENV = frozenset({"PGHOST", "PG_BIN"})


def check_environment():
    rejected = sorted(name for name in os.environ
                      if name.startswith("PG") and name not in ALLOWED_PG_ENV)
    if rejected:
        # Never echo values: these may contain passwords or service credentials.
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing implicit PostgreSQL environment: " + ", ".join(rejected))


def child_environment():
    # Do not mutate os.environ: D03 can open connections from multiple threads.
    return {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items()
            if not name.startswith("PG") and name != "DATABASE_URL"}


def run(*args, check=True):
    result = subprocess.run(args, check=False, text=True, capture_output=True,
                            env=child_environment())
    if check and result.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{Path(args[0]).name} exited {result.returncode}:\n"
            f"{result.stdout}{result.stderr}"
        )
    return result


def load_state():
    if STATE.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing a symlink state file")
    if not STATE.exists():
        raise RuntimeError("No owned cluster. Run labctl.py start first")
    state = json.loads(STATE.read_text())
    root = Path(state["root"])
    if root.is_symlink() or root.resolve().parent != Path("/tmp").resolve():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing a cluster outside the owned /tmp root")
    if not root.name.startswith("lsdb-"):
        raise RuntimeError("Unexpected cluster directory name")
    metadata = root.stat()
    if metadata.st_uid != os.getuid() or stat.S_IMODE(metadata.st_mode) != 0o700:
        raise RuntimeError("Cluster root must be owned by this OS user, mode 0700")
    marker = root / MARKER
    if marker.is_symlink() or json.loads(marker.read_text()) != state:
        raise RuntimeError("Ownership marker mismatch; no database action performed")
    if state["lab"] != str(LAB):
        raise RuntimeError("This cluster belongs to a different lab directory")
    for child in ("data", "socket"):
        path = root / child
        if path.is_symlink() or path.resolve().parent != root.resolve():
            raise RuntimeError("Refusing redirected cluster paths")
    return state


def empty_passfile(state):
    # Also works for previously created, marker-checked clusters. Never consult
    # HOME/.pgpass; never follow a passfile symlink or reuse nonempty credentials.
    path = Path(state["root"]) / "empty.pgpass"
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK, 0o600)
    try:
        metadata = os.fstat(fd)
        if (not stat.S_ISREG(metadata.st_mode) or metadata.st_uid != os.getuid()
                or stat.S_IMODE(metadata.st_mode) != 0o600 or metadata.st_size != 0):
            raise RuntimeError("Refusing unsafe lab passfile")
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    return str(path)


def raw_dsn(state, admin=False):
    check_environment()
    return make_conninfo(
        host=str(Path(state["root"]) / "socket"), port=state["port"],
        dbname="langshift_lab", user=state["admin"] if admin else "lab_student",
        passfile=empty_passfile(state),
        connect_timeout=3, application_name=LAB.name,
        options="-c timezone=UTC -c statement_timeout=8000 -c lock_timeout=3000",
    )


def check_pid_file(state):
    root = Path(state["root"])
    pid_file = root / "data/postmaster.pid"
    if pid_file.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing redirected PID file")
    if pid_file.exists():
        lines = pid_file.read_text().splitlines()
        if (Path(lines[1]).resolve() != (root / "data").resolve()
                or lines[3] != str(state["port"])
                or Path(lines[4]).resolve() != (root / "socket").resolve()):
            raise RuntimeError("PID file does not describe the owned server")


def verify_server(state):
    check_environment()
    check_pid_file(state)
    with psycopg.connect(raw_dsn(state, admin=True), autocommit=True) as conn:
        actual = conn.execute("""
            SELECT current_setting('data_directory'),
                   current_setting('server_version_num')::int,
                   system_identifier::text
            FROM pg_control_system()
        """).fetchone()
    if (Path(actual[0]).resolve() != Path(state["root"]) / "data"
            or actual[1] != VERSION_NUM
            or actual[2] != state["system_identifier"]):
        raise RuntimeError("Wrong server identity/version; refusing SQL")


def connect(*, autocommit=False):
    check_environment()
    state = load_state()
    verify_server(state)
    return psycopg.connect(raw_dsn(state), autocommit=autocommit)


def start():
    check_environment()
    if STATE.exists() or STATE.is_symlink():
        state = load_state()
        check_pid_file(state)
        result = run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                     str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "status", check=False)
        if result.returncode == 3:
            run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "-l",
                str(Path(state["root"]) / "server.log"), "-w", "-t", "15", "start")
        elif result.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
        verify_server(state)
        print("owned cluster ready (existing data retained)")
        return
    default = Path(shutil.which("initdb") or "/opt/homebrew/bin/initdb").parent
    pg_bin = Path(os.environ.get("PG_BIN", str(default))).resolve()
    for tool in ("postgres", "initdb", "pg_ctl", "psql"):
        version = run(str(pg_bin / tool), "--version").stdout.strip()
        if " 18.6" not in version:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Expected PostgreSQL 18.6: {version}")
    root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="lsdb-", dir="/tmp")).resolve()
    root.chmod(0o700)
    (root / "socket").mkdir(mode=0o700)
    state = {
        "root": str(root), "lab": str(LAB), "token": secrets.token_hex(16),
        "admin": "lab_admin_" + secrets.token_hex(6), "pg_bin": str(pg_bin),
        "port": 49152 + secrets.randbelow(12000),
    }
    # Persist ownership before starting so partial failures remain recoverable.
    def save():
        text = json.dumps(state, indent=2) + "\n"
        (root / MARKER).write_text(text)
        STATE.write_text(text)
        STATE.chmod(0o600)
    save()
    try:
        run(str(pg_bin / "initdb"), "-D", str(root / "data"), "-U", state["admin"],
            "--auth-local=trust", "--auth-host=reject", "--encoding=UTF8", "--no-locale")
        with (root / "data/postgresql.conf").open("a") as config:
            config.write(f"\nlisten_addresses = ''\nport = {state['port']}\n")
            config.write(f"unix_socket_directories = '{root / 'socket'}'\n")
            config.write("unix_socket_permissions = 0700\ntimezone = 'UTC'\n")
        run(str(pg_bin / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(root / "data"), "-l",
            str(root / "server.log"), "-w", "-t", "15", "start")
        admin_dsn = make_conninfo(raw_dsn(state, admin=True), dbname="postgres")
        with psycopg.connect(admin_dsn, autocommit=True) as conn:
            state["system_identifier"] = conn.execute(
                "SELECT system_identifier::text FROM pg_control_system()"
            ).fetchone()[0]
            save()
            conn.execute("CREATE ROLE lab_student LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE")
            conn.execute("CREATE DATABASE langshift_lab OWNER lab_student")
        verify_server(state)
    except BaseException:
        # This exact new root was allocated above; never stop any default service.
        run(str(pg_bin / "pg_ctl"), "-D", str(root / "data"),
            "-m", "fast", "-w", "-t", "15", "stop", check=False)
        raise
    print("owned cluster ready: PostgreSQL 18.6; TCP disabled")
    print(f"root={root}")


def reset():
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tasks, project_members, projects, users")
        conn.execute((LAB / "sql/schema.sql").read_text())
        conn.execute((LAB / "sql/seed.sql").read_text())


def stop():
    state = load_state()
    check_pid_file(state)
    pg_ctl = str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl")
    data = str(Path(state["root"]) / "data")
    result = run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "status", check=False)
    if result.returncode == 3:
        print("owned cluster already stopped; files retained")
        return
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
    # Keep the identity check, but run it in a clean child so a poisoned shell
    # cannot prevent cleanup. No process-global environment mutation/race, and
    # no SQL against any target other than this lab's marker-checked socket.
    run(sys.executable, str(LAB / "labctl.py"), "dsn")
    print(run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "-m", "fast", "-w", "-t", "15", "stop").stdout.strip())
    if run(pg_ctl, "-D", data, "status", check=False).returncode != 3:
        raise RuntimeError("Owned server did not stop")
    print("owned cluster stopped; pg_ctl status=3; files retained")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("command", choices=["start", "status", "dsn", "reset", "stop", "psql"])
    parser.add_argument("--yes-reset", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--file")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command not in {"stop", "status"}:
        check_environment()
    if args.command == "start":
        start()
    elif args.command == "stop":
        stop()
    elif args.command == "reset":
        if not args.yes_reset:
            parser.error("reset destroys only this lab's tables; require --yes-reset")
        reset()
        print("schema + seed ready: users=2 projects=3 members=4 tasks=5")
    elif args.command == "status":
        state = load_state()
        check_pid_file(state)
        result = run(str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "pg_ctl"), "-D",
                     str(Path(state["root"]) / "data"), "status", check=False)
        if result.returncode not in (0, 3):
            raise RuntimeError(result.stderr or result.stdout)
        print(json.dumps({"root": state["root"], "running": result.returncode == 0,
                          "pg_ctl_status": result.returncode}))
    else:
        state = load_state()
        verify_server(state)
        if args.command == "dsn":
            print(raw_dsn(state))
        else:
            command = [str(Path(state["pg_bin"]) / "psql"), "-X", "-w", raw_dsn(state),
                       "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-P", "pager=off"]
            if args.file:
                command += ["-f", str(Path(args.file).resolve())]
            subprocess.run(command, check=True, env=child_environment())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
